best_for: Staff whose company runs on Webex, and people who host short calls of up to 100 guests and can live with a 40-minute cap.
description:
Webex is Cisco's app for video meetings, calls and team chat. It is closed-source software, and signing up for the free plan takes no credit card or other payment details.

Once you have an account, you invite people from the app and they get an email with a link to download it. Guests do not need a license of their own to join, and in most cases they can join from a web browser without installing anything. You can call into a meeting over the internet from your computer. The desktop app is needed for some features, such as dialing a regular phone number. Each account runs one call or meeting on one device at a time.

points.title: Free stops at 40 minutes
points.text: Webex Free costs nothing and allows unlimited meetings, but each one ends at 40 minutes and holds up to 100 attendees. It includes screen sharing, whiteboards, local recording, noise removal and messaging.

points.title: Paid plans go through sales
points.text: The pricing page lists only the free plan with a price. Enterprise, with up to 1,000 attendees, cloud recording and the AI Assistant, is quoted by sales, and paid features need a host license for each person who uses them. You can drop back to Free at any time. Plans were read on the date below.

points.title: macOS 13 or newer
points.text: Cisco's requirements page puts the Mac minimum at macOS 13, and the Mac downloads listed here declare the same, in separate Intel and Apple silicon builds. Windows needs Windows 10 or later, or Windows Server 2016.

points.title: Blurred backgrounds need memory
points.text: The base requirement is 4 GB of RAM. Virtual or blurred backgrounds on Windows need 8 GB or more, and machines with a dedicated GPU need at least 2 GB of video memory for them.

points.title: Pick user or machine install
points.text: The Windows builds come as MSI packages for x64 and Arm64, each in a per-user and an all-users form. The per-user one suits a laptop without admin rights; IT can push the machine-wide one.

points.title: Downgrades are a Windows thing here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 54 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so an older Mac build needs another source. Cisco also publishes a Linux client, which this site does not list.
